properties.name: Mount Whitney
properties.description: Highest summit in the contiguous United States (14,505 ft). Towering sheer granite peak on the Sierra Crest above Whitney Portal and Lone Pine.

properties.name: Mount Williamson
properties.description: Second-highest peak in California (14,379 ft); imposing granite fortress rising dramatically over Owens Valley.

properties.name: North Palisade
properties.description: Third-highest peak in the Sierra Nevada (14,248 ft); home to Palisade Glacier, the largest glacier in the Sierra.

properties.name: Mount Langley
properties.description: Southernmost Sierra fourteener; a straightforward class 1-2 ascent from the Cottonwood Lakes basin.

properties.name: Mount Kaweah
properties.description: Dark metamorphic giant of the Great Western Divide, towering over the Big Arroyo on the High Sierra Trail.

properties.name: Mount Darwin
properties.description: Highest peak of the Evolution group, rising above the JMT's Evolution Basin and Muir Pass.

properties.name: Mount Goddard
properties.description: Dark, isolated summit at the head of Goddard Canyon in Kings Canyon National Park.

properties.name: Mount Humphreys
properties.description: Bishop's skyline giant, the highest peak between the Palisades and Yosemite.

properties.name: Temple Crag
properties.description: Iconic castle-like granite spire rising 3,000 feet directly above turquoise Second and Third Big Pine Lakes.

properties.name: Half Dome
properties.description: World-famous glaciated granite monolith rising 4,800 feet above Yosemite Valley floor. Ascended via the historic cable route.

properties.name: El Capitan
properties.description: World's most celebrated 3,000-foot sheer vertical granite wall in Yosemite Valley; global mecca of big-wall rock climbing.

properties.name: Clouds Rest
properties.description: Knife-edge granite crest towering 1,000 ft above Half Dome with a sheer 4,500-ft drop into Tenaya Canyon.

properties.name: Mount Hoffmann
properties.description: Geographic center of Yosemite National Park with a summit panorama over Tuolumne and the Clark Range.

properties.name: Mount Conness
properties.description: Granite peak with a hanging glacier on the Yosemite crest north of Tioga Pass.

properties.name: Mount Lyell
properties.description: Highest peak in Yosemite National Park (13,114 ft); carries the park's largest remaining ice mass, Lyell Glacier.

properties.name: Mount Dana
properties.description: Second-highest peak in Yosemite, standing above Tioga Pass with reddish metamorphic rock and views across Mono Lake.

properties.name: Mount Ritter
properties.description: Highest summit of the dark volcanic Ritter Range, first climbed by John Muir in 1872.

properties.name: Banner Peak
properties.description: Spectacular jagged volcanic horn towering directly over Thousand Island Lake in the Ansel Adams Wilderness.

properties.name: Matterhorn Peak
properties.description: Sawtooth Ridge's signature horn, made famous by Kerouac's 'The Dharma Bums'.

properties.name: White Mountain Peak
properties.description: Third-highest peak in California, rising above the Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest across Owens Valley.

properties.name: Alta Peak
properties.description: Sequoia National Park summit with sweeping views of the Great Western Divide and Mount Whitney.

properties.name: Moro Rock
properties.description: Granite dome above Giant Forest climbed by 350 stairs; 6,000-ft view down to the Kaweah foothills.

properties.name: Mount Tallac
properties.description: Premier peak in the Lake Tahoe Basin (9,735 ft); prominent snow cross on its northeast face overlooking Fallen Leaf Lake.

properties.name: Pyramid Peak
properties.description: Highest point in Desolation Wilderness, a steep granite pyramid above Highway 50 and the Crystal Range.

properties.name: Mount Rose
properties.description: Dominant volcanic peak of North Lake Tahoe (10,776 ft); spectacular alpine winter skiing and 360-degree desert/lake vistas.

properties.name: Freel Peak
properties.description: Highest point in the Lake Tahoe Basin (10,881 ft), perched on the Carson Range southeast of South Lake Tahoe.

properties.name: Round Top
properties.description: Jagged volcanic neck rising above Carson Pass and Winnemucca Lake in the Mokelumne Wilderness; premier summer wildflower basin.

properties.name: Sierra Buttes
properties.description: Jagged volcanic crown of the northern Sierra with a stair-access fire lookout above the Sardine Lakes.

properties.name: Lassen Peak
properties.description: One of the world's largest plug dome volcanoes (10,457 ft); last erupted in 1915, creating the Devastated Area.

properties.name: Brokeoff Mountain
properties.description: Remnant of the ancient Mount Tehama stratovolcano on the southwest corner of Lassen Volcanic NP.

properties.name: Mount Shasta
properties.description: Dominant potentially active stratovolcano rising 14,179 feet; glaciated northern California landmark visible from 150 miles away.

properties.name: Mount Eddy
properties.description: Highest peak in the Klamath Mountains, with the best summit view of Mount Shasta (via the PCT and Deadfall Lakes).

properties.name: Thompson Peak
properties.description: Highest mountain in the Trinity Alps (9,002 ft); rugged glaciated white granite peak with Thompson Glacier.

properties.name: Snow Mountain East
properties.description: Highest point of the Mendocino National Forest and the inner Coast Range above Clear Lake.

properties.name: Mount Saint Helena
properties.description: Volcanic high point of the Mayacamas Mountains where Robert Louis Stevenson honeymooned in 1880.

properties.name: Mount Diablo
properties.description: Bay Area sentinel (3,849 ft); viewshed encompassing 40,000 square miles across 40 California counties from Sierra to Farallons.

properties.name: Mount Tamalpais (East Peak)
properties.description: The Sleeping Lady (2,571 ft); legendary Marin County summit with sweeping 360° views of San Francisco, Farallon Islands, and Mt. Diablo.

properties.name: Mount Wittenberg
properties.description: Highest point in Point Reyes National Seashore, on Inverness Ridge above Bear Valley.

properties.name: Mission Peak
properties.description: Fremont's iconic grassy summit with its photogenic 'Peak Post' and views over the South Bay.

properties.name: Mount Hamilton
properties.description: Diablo Range summit crowned by the historic Lick Observatory (1888) above San José.

properties.name: Mount Umunhum
properties.description: Santa Cruz Mountains summit with the restored Cold War radar 'Cube' and Bay-to-Monterey views.

properties.name: Junipero Serra Peak
properties.description: Highest point of the Santa Lucia Range in the Ventana Wilderness, with sugar pines on its summit.

properties.name: Cone Peak
properties.description: One of the steepest coastal gradients in North America; rises 5,155 feet above the Pacific Ocean in just three horizontal miles.

properties.name: Fremont Peak
properties.description: Gavilan Range high point (3,169 ft) above Salinas with clear panoramas across Monterey Bay, Salinas Valley, and Santa Cruz.

properties.name: Lake Tahoe
properties.description: Second-deepest lake in the US (1,645 ft deep) and largest alpine lake in North America. World-famous for cobalt-blue water clarity.

properties.name: Emerald Bay
properties.description: Glacial fjord on Lake Tahoe's southwest shore; National Natural Landmark featuring Fannette Island, the only island in Lake Tahoe.

properties.name: Fallen Leaf Lake
properties.description: Deep glacial lake tucked beneath Mount Tallac; pristine waters, aspen groves, and gateway to Desolation Wilderness.

properties.name: Lake Aloha
properties.description: Spectacular shallow alpine reservoir in Desolation Wilderness dotted with hundreds of glaciated white granite islands.

properties.name: Donner Lake
properties.description: Historic Sierra passage lake ringed by ponderosa pines; popular for sailing, beach camping, and Emigrant Trail history.

properties.name: Caples Lake
properties.description: Carson Pass reservoir beneath the Mokelumne Wilderness; trout fishing and trailheads to Emigrant Lake.

properties.name: Mono Lake
properties.description: Ancient saline soda lake (over 1 million years old); famed for dramatic limestone tufa towers and nesting home to millions of migratory birds.

properties.name: Tenaya Lake
properties.description: 'Jewel of the High Sierra' along Tioga Pass Road in Yosemite; crystal-clear granite beach ringed by glaciated domes.

properties.name: Thousand Island Lake
properties.description: Island-studded lake beneath Banner Peak on the PCT; one of Ansel Adams' most famous subjects.

properties.name: June Lake & Gull Lake
properties.description: Heart of the scenic June Lake Loop in the Eastern Sierra; horseshoe-shaped glacial canyon with trout fishing and fall foliage.

properties.name: Convict Lake
properties.description: Dramatic alpine lake framed by the striped, near-vertical geology of Mount Morrison; world-class trout fishing and autumn aspens.

properties.name: Lake Mary (Mammoth Lakes Basin)
properties.description: Largest of the Mammoth Lakes Basin lakes, ringed by campgrounds and trailheads to Duck Pass and Crystal Lake.

properties.name: Big Pine Lakes
properties.description: Chain of seven vibrant turquoise glacial lakes fed by the meltwaters of Palisade Glacier in the high John Muir Wilderness.

properties.name: Lake Sabrina
properties.description: Granite-bound Bishop Creek reservoir famed for golden aspen color and trailheads to Blue Lake and Dingleberry Lake.

properties.name: Rae Lakes
properties.description: Necklace of granite lakes beneath Fin Dome on the JMT and Rae Lakes Loop in Kings Canyon NP.

properties.name: Hume Lake
properties.description: Historic 1908 log-flume lake in Giant Sequoia NM between Grant Grove and Kings Canyon.

properties.name: Huntington Lake
properties.description: Sierra National Forest's sailing and camping lake beneath the Kaiser Wilderness.

properties.name: Bass Lake
properties.description: Warm-water recreation lake just south of Yosemite's Wawona entrance.

properties.name: Pinecrest Lake
properties.description: Family lake in the Stanislaus NF along Highway 108 with a 4-mile shoreline loop trail.

properties.name: Manzanita Lake
properties.description: Classic reflection lake in Lassen Volcanic National Park; crystal-clear surface capturing the iconic reflection of Lassen Peak.

properties.name: Lake Almanor
properties.description: Large mountain reservoir in the Lassen NF with Lassen Peak views and the PCT passing nearby at Chester.

properties.name: Bucks Lake
properties.description: Plumas NF lake beside the Bucks Lake Wilderness and the PCT.

properties.name: Shasta Lake
properties.description: Largest reservoir in California with 365 miles of shoreline; nestled in forested canyons beneath snow-capped Mount Shasta.

properties.name: Trinity Lake
properties.description: California's third-largest reservoir (Clair Engle Lake) beneath the Trinity Alps; quiet coves, houseboats, and USFS campgrounds.

properties.name: Whiskeytown Lake
properties.description: Crystal-clear reservoir in the Shasta-Cascade ringed by pine-clad mountains and cascading waterfalls.

properties.name: Lake Siskiyou
properties.description: Reservoir at the base of Mount Shasta with the classic mirror view of the mountain.

properties.name: Castle Lake
properties.description: Glacial cirque lake beneath Castle Crags' granite, trailhead for Heart Lake.

properties.name: Clear Lake
properties.description: Largest natural freshwater lake wholly in California and possibly the oldest lake in North America.

properties.name: Lake Berryessa
properties.description: Massive warm-water reservoir in eastern Napa County hills; renowned for boating, bass fishing, and the famed 'Glory Hole' spillway.

properties.name: Lake Oroville
properties.description: California's second-largest reservoir behind the tallest dam in the US, with Feather Falls in its watershed.

properties.name: Folsom Lake
properties.description: Sacramento-area reservoir at the confluence of the North and South Forks of the American River.
